text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Romania is running behind the Visegrad group, a recent EBRD survvey showed. The recent report of transition countries from Eastern and Central Europe presents a economic comparision between Romania and other ex-communist countries. The report said industrial output and inflation will rise by 4.6 percent and 60 percent in 1996.

- The newspaper presents an interview with Josef Simon, president of the Romania-Switzerland Chamber of Commerce in which he suggests what what the next government should to do to lure foreign investment.
- The fate of Romania's troubled private bank Credit Bank will be decided next year.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The present energy reserves, reported by the Industry Minister, are: 8.1 million tonnes of coal; 674,000 tonnes of fuel oil and one billion cubic metres of natural gas.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- In the case of a hard winter, coal supplies will be enough for only 70 days.
- Winlook Management Zurich consortium announces conditions for investing in troubled Romanian bank Dacia Felix. The swiss consortium hopes a new government will cooperate with them.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA:

- The centrist's Democratic Convention (CDR) presidential candidate Emil Constantinescu said that the new government emerging from general elections will not exact revenge against its defeated opponents.
- The victory of Romania's opposition in parliamentary polls increase the chances of admission to NATO in the first wave of expansion to be announced next year.
- The paper says President Ion Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) wants him to win the run-off in the presidential election on November 17 at any price.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper announces a boycott of news about the PDSR activity after a senior party member said it had been wrong to develop freedom of the press.
- During his campaign visit in Galati the President Ion Iliescu was met by hecklers.
ADEVARUL
- Ion Iliescu and Emil Constantinescu will have two final debates on state television next week.
- Emil Constantinescu says Iliescu, elected to the Senate in last week's parliamentary election, will make a good leader in the upper chamber.
JURNALUL NATIONAL

- The National Pesaint Party (PNTCD), the main party of Constantinescu's Democratic Convention, has decided on the procedure to appoint the Prime Minister. The negociations on this appointment will begin on November 19.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
